To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the functional consequences of missense NF1-GRDs have been determined and that 10 of 15 mutations were found to be pathogenic, while five were deemed to be nonpathogenic.
15 missense NF1 mutations were identified, 10 of which were found to be pathogenic and five of which were found not to be pathogenic.
10 of 15 missense mutations of the GTPase activating protein (GAP) domain of neurofibromin (the neurofibromatose 1 (NF1)-encoded protein) are potentially pathogenic.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and functional characterization of novel and previously reported missense mutations in the GRD of the neurofibroma tumor suppressor protein, neurofibroma.
the identification and characterization of NF1- GRD mutations that are potentially pathogenic and thus likely to be of relevance to the diagnosis of NF1.
the identification and characterization of NF1- GRD variants that are potentially pathogenic and may therefore be of clinical importance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
10/15 NF1-GRDs were potentially pathogenic, whereas the remaining five variants are unlikely to be of clinical significance.
10 of the 15 missense mutations identified within the NF1- GRD were potentially pathogenic, whereas five were not.
all 15 NF1-GRDs tested in this study were either of uncertain or of probable pathogenicity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the NF1- GRD variants p.R1204G and p.R1276G, p.L1302R, p.T1323N, p.E1336G, p.E1354G, p.V1368D and p.K1409Q, are potentially pathogenic, whereas the NF1-GRP variants p.R1206W, p.I1308V, p.Q1334R, p.R1396G and p.S1470F are not.
15 missense NF1-GRDs were assessed and 10 were deemed pathogenic and 5 were not.
10/15 NF1-GRDs are potentially pathogenic, 5/15 are unlikely to be pathogenic, and the remaining 5/15 require further investigation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
missense mutations in the NF1 gene can be assessed for pathogenicity by the simple functional assay we describe.
the NF1-GRP domain is a critical region of the NF1 protein, and that mutations affecting this region may have a high likelihood of pathogenicity.
missense mutations in the NF1 gene should be considered as potentially pathogenic and that functional analysis should be performed to assess their potential pathogenicity.
